rules.rule_name: Write should have, not should of
rules.rule_description: Would of, could of, should of, must of and might of are mishearings of the contracted have.
rules.incorrect_example: The dose should of been lower.
rules.corrected_example: The dose should have been lower.
rules.explanation: Modal verbs take have, not of.
rules.exception_conditions: Quoted speech or a phrase such as “may of” in a different sense.
rules.suggested_correction: Replace the match with: \1 have
rules.editor_message: Write should have, not should of. Modal verbs take have, not of.

rules.rule_name: Remove to after a modal verb
rules.rule_description: A modal verb is followed by the base verb without to.

rules.corrected_example: Patients can choose a clinic.
rules.exception_conditions: The noun will (the will to live) and can (a tin can to carry).
rules.suggested_correction: Replace the match with: \1
rules.editor_message: Remove to after a modal verb. Modals take the bare infinitive.

rules.rule_subcategory: modal plus a verb ending in s

rules.editor_message: Use the base form after a modal, not an -s form. A modal takes the base form.

rules.editor_message: Use the base form after a modal, not a past form. A modal takes the base form.

rules.rule_name: Use the past participle after have, has and had

rules.corrected_example: The team has gone to the site.

rules.suggested_correction: Edit as in the corrected example; the editor decides.
rules.editor_message: Use the past participle after have, has and had. The perfect tenses take the past participle.

rules.rule_name: Use the simple past after a subject pronoun
rules.rule_description: A subject pronoun directly followed by seen, done, gone and similar participles lacks an auxiliary.

rules.corrected_example: We saw a large effect.
rules.explanation: Either an auxiliary or the past form is needed.

rules.editor_message: Use the simple past after a subject pronoun. Either an auxiliary or the past form is needed.

rules.rule_name: Do not use the passive with an intransitive verb

rules.corrected_example: The error occurred during transfer.
rules.exception_conditions: “Has been occurred” also matches (leaving has occurred).
rules.suggested_correction: Replace the match with: \1
rules.editor_message: Do not use the passive with an intransitive verb. Intransitive verbs cannot be passive.

rules.rule_subcategory: did not plus a past form
rules.rule_name: Use the base form after did not, does not and do not

rules.editor_message: Use the base form after did not, does not and do not. The auxiliary carries the tense.

rules.rule_subcategory: does not plus a verb ending in s

rules.rule_name: Use the base verb after to
rules.rule_description: An infinitive with to takes the base form.

rules.rule_subcategory: let or make plus object plus to

rules.rule_name: Write used to for a past habit
rules.rule_description: A past habit is used to, not use to.

rules.rule_name: Use had in the if clause of a past conditional
rules.rule_description: A past conditional is if plus had, then would have.

rules.explanation: Would does not belong in the if clause.

rules.editor_message: Use had in the if clause of a past conditional. Would does not belong in the if clause.

rules.rule_name: Use the participle after has been
rules.rule_description: Has been show, has been use and similar forms need a participle.

rules.explanation: After been a participle is needed.

rules.rule_name: Use the participle after is, are, was and were
rules.rule_description: A passive needs a participle: were collected, not were collect.

rules.rule_subcategory: present perfect with a past time
rules.rule_name: Use the simple past with a finished time
rules.rule_description: Has collected last week mixes the present perfect with a finished time.
rules.incorrect_example: The sample has been collected last week.
rules.corrected_example: The sample was collected last week.
rules.explanation: A finished time takes the simple past.
rules.exception_conditions: A time after a break (has been collected, as noted last week).
rules.suggested_correction: Edit as in the corrected example; the editor decides.
rules.editor_message: Use the simple past with a finished time. A finished time takes the simple past.
rules.false_positive_risks: A comma may separate the time phrase.

rules.rule_name: Use the correct irregular past form

rules.rule_description: A passive with an agent (was completed by the participants) can often be active.

rules.rule_name: Keep one tense within a passage

rules.rule_subcategory: gerund or infinitive with a change of meaning
rules.rule_name: Check stop, remember and try plus a verb

rules.rule_description: Can denotes ability; may denotes permission or possibility. Modern usage accepts can for permission.

rules.suggested_correction: Edit as in the corrected example; the editor decides.
rules.editor_message: Use may or might for possibility, will for certainty. The modal states how sure the author is.
rules.source_reference: Compiler’s knowledge of standard English usage. Not checked against a published usage guide.

rules.rule_description: After between, except, with, to and similar prepositions the object form is used.

rules.rule_name: Use I in a compound subject
